PANG , Managing Editor July 24, 2026 COURTESY OF WIKIMEDIA COMMONS Mike Pence, former vice president of the United States and governor of Indiana. Editor’s note: The opinions expressed in this column reflect the views of the author, not The Daily Evergreen. The Foley Institute’s decision to honor former vice president and Indiana governor Mike Pence not only leaves me scratching my head, but is also a slap in the face to the communities WSU has claimed to support and uplift. Pence’s policies have continuously hurt women, LGBTQ+ communities and at-risk youth, the very communities WSU has claimed to support while honoring a man who has built a political career on hiding behind religion as justification for bigotry and ignorance. Even by the Foley Institute’s own criteria, including commitment to ethical leadership, integrity, bipartisanship and democratic values, the decision to honor Pence is truly bewildering. “He demonstrated remarkable integrity, courage and a commitment to upholding democratic norms in the face of pressures to block or delay the certification of the 2020 election,” said Cornell Clayton, director of the Foley Institute. While it is true Pence ultimately refused to capitulate to Donald Trump’s blatantly unconstitutional orders to overturn the election by refusing to certify the votes, what Clayton fails to consider is everything that led up to that point. By now, it is widely known Pence repeatedly consulted Dan Quayle, former vice president under George H. W. Bush, on his decision leading up to Jan. 6. On several occasions, Pence pressed Quayle on whether there was anything he could do to overturn the results of the election, to which Quayle had to repeatedly tell Pence there was nothing he could do. It is clear Pence’s decision – if you can call it that, given the vice president’s role in the matter is purely ceremonial – was not some strict moral and ethical line Pence was drawing in the sand. Make no mistake, he repeatedly looked for ways to justify betraying the Constitution, the American people and basic democratic values to remain in power. Even if Pence had drawn a hard and fast line in the sand on the basis of inherent objections to overturning a democratic election, that still should not be enough to earn an award. The vice president’s ceremonial role in the certification of the votes is just that: ceremonial. If we are just handing out awards now to people who do not violate the Constitution by overstepping their constitutional authority, might I suggest another recipient: William Henry Harrison, whose most egregious error as president was perhaps thinking he could beat the weather. Then, in the aftermath of the Jan. 6 insurrection, Pence spinelessly declined to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove Trump from power. Even after Trump encouraged his supporters to storm the Capitol and for hours refused to tell supporters to stand down, Pence failed to act to protect the American people and the sanctity of the presidency. Looking past Pence’s involvement in the 2020 election, it remains clear he is not some champion of integrity and democratic values. By the morning Joe Biden and Kamala Harris were declared the projected winners of the 2020 election, the Trump administration had already been embroiled in almost four years of scandals. From the very start of the Trump administration, the White House was plagued by scandal after scandal as Pence stood idly by, that is when he was not directly involved himself. Even before Trump and Pence were sworn in, the Trump-Pence ticket faced national backlash after a 2005 recording of Donald Trump bragging about sexually assaulting women was published by the Washington Post. The tape was published by the Washington Post in October 2016, a month before the 2016 election. A man of integrity, Christian or not, would not dare associate with a man who not only admitted to sexually assaulting women, but also bragged about it publicly. Yet, Pence stood by him. Mind you, these were not mere accusations of wrongdoing. It was audio recording of Trump himself bragging about how he can get away with rape because he is rich and powerful. Then there is Trump’s first impeachment. Trump was impeached by the U.S. House of Representatives in December 2019 after it became clear Trump intentionally withheld military aid to Ukraine as leverage to pressure Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to investigate political rival Joe Biden. Though Pence was relegated to a minor character during this scandal at the time, it is preposterous to assume the President’s right-hand man, who Trump had already sent to Ukraine and Poland for “diplomatic discussions,” had no part in the efforts to pressure Ukraine for partisan political gain. Even if we were to accept Pence was uninvolved and initially unaware, which again, would be a ridiculous concession, it has to be said that an honorable man of integrity and commitment to democratic values would not stand idly by after his boss is impeached for pulling a play out of Putin’s personal playbook. Regardless of how involved and aware Pence was, it is clear Pence failed to faithfully execute his oath of office. It was Pence’s duty and commitment to the Constitution and the American people to be aware and do the right thing, and he failed. This is Pence’s legacy, a legacy of destructive policy and cowardice. He is not a man of high moral and ethical integrity, nor is he a champion of democratic values. The Foley Institute’s decision to honor Pence is a decision to stamp his legacy with a seal of approval, a seal that irreparably ties this university, its administration and its students to a dark and unfortunate era of American government. The decision to honor Pence is a betrayal to communities WSU claims to support. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/11/magy.text: Menü Kereső Kijött a közlöny: augusztus 19-től új köztársasági elnöke van Magyarországnak Belföld Weiler Vilmos Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kedden este megjelent a Magyar Közlöny idei 109. száma , amely egyetlen országgyűlési határozatot tartalmaz: azt, amely szerint Országgyűlés Baka Andrást választotta Magyarország köztársasági elnökévé. A határozat elfogadásakor lépett hatályba, az államfő azonban csak augusztus 19-én lép hivatalba. A közlöny vonatkozó része így néz ki: Forrás: Magyar Közlöny Baka Andrást, a Legfelsőbb Bíróság volt elnökét kedden 140 igen, 6 nem és nulla tartózkodás mellett, titkos szavazással választották meg Magyarország köztársasági elnökévé. A Fidesz és a KDNP már korábban közölte, hogy nem vesz részt az új államfő megválasztásában. De ki is Baka András, aki egy ilyen éles és konfliktusos helyzetben veszi át az államfői posztot? Baka András az emberi jogi, kisebbségi jogi kérdések kutatója. Neve akkor vált különösen ismertté, amikor 2011-ben jogellenesen eltávolították a Legfelsőbb Bíróság éléről, miután bírálta az Orbán-rendszer igazságszolgáltatás átalakítására vonatkozó terveit. Baka András 1952-ben született Budapesten. 1978-ban az ELTE Állam- és Jogtudományi Karán szerzett jogi doktorátust, majd több mint húsz éven át a Magyar Tudományos Akadémia (MTA) Állam- és Jogtudományi Intézetének tudományos kutatójaként dolgozott, később az Államigazgatási Főiskola főigazgatójaként tevékenykedett. 1991 és 2008 között két cikluson át volt az Emberi Jogok Európai Bíróságának bírája. Az 1980-as évektől az Egyesült Államok több egyetemén volt vendégprofesszor, és többször hívták meg előadni Franciaországba és az NSZK-ba is. Baka a rendszerváltás utáni első parlamenti ciklus elején, 1990–1991-ben az MDF országgyűlési képviselője volt, de a pártba nem lépett be. Szakszervezeti múlttal is rendelkezik: 1988–1990 között a Tudományos Dolgozók Szakszervezetének (TUDOSZ), 1989–1990 között az Értelmiségi Szakszervezeti Tömörülésnek (ÉSZT) volt az elnöke. Baka 2016 júniusában jogerősen pert nyert az Emberi Jogok Legfelsőbb Bíróságán. A testület megállapította, hogy Baka András főbírót azért menesztették idő előtt személyre szabott jogalkotással a tisztségéből, mert szakmai minőségében nyilvánosan kritizálta a bíróságok függetlenségét veszélyeztető lépéseket. Később az Európa Tanács Miniszteri Bizottsága felelősségre vonta a magyar államot azért, mert 2016 óta nem hajtotta végre a Baka kontra Magyarország ügyben hozott strasbourgi ítéletet. https://www.dw.com/en/taiwan-typhoon-cha.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Oc9d More than 500 people were injured as Typhoon Champi swept through Taiwan Image: cnsphoto/REUTERS Advertisement Typhoon Champi killed at least one person and left more than 500 people with injuries as it passed through Taiwan on Saturday. Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at 1, after a man was swept ​away by waves from the island of Liuqiu. At least 527 others were injured during the heavy wind and torrential rain. Several parts in Taiwan received heavy rain and strong winds that prompted authorities to cut off power, leaving thousands of people without power supply. Some 280,000 households were knocked out of power, according to United Daily News, a local Taiwanese newspaper. By Saturday morning, the power supply was restored to 80% of the households. Despite weakening, Champi is still packing strong winds near its center Image: I-Hwa Cheng/AFP Champi also led to 259 flights cancellations, an improvement from Friday, ⁠when ​the number was almost 1,000, the Transport Ministry said. Several trees were downed amid strong gusts In the capital Taipei. Authorities in several districts of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday. Champi headed to China The typhoon continued to weaken as it moved north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there. Chinese authorities have sent a team to ​the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi ⁠approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. Schools and offices were closed in several districts in Taiwan because of Champi Image: I-Hwa Cheng/AFP It said it had readied 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment, ⁠while more than 41,000 firefighters were on ​emergency duty. Typhoon Champi started out as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year. While it is weakening, Champi is still packing ​gusts of around 78 km/h (126 mph) near its center, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).
